items.d: 에스와이폴라리스는 KB국민카드, 항공권 예약 플랫폼 와이페이모어와 AI 에이전트가 고객을 대신해 항공권을 예약하고 결제하는 공동 실증(PoC)을 진행하고 있다고 25일 밝혔다. 실증에는 와이페이모어가 가맹점으로 참여해, AI 에이전트가 고객의 요청에 따라 항공권을 조회하고 결제하는 과정을 세 회사가 함께 검증한다. 세 회사는 기존 카드사의 인증·결제 체계를 기반으로 AI 에이전트 결제의 적용 가능성을 검증하고, 고객정보 보호와 안전한 결제 환경
items.fullText: 경제 금융 에스와이폴라리스-KB국민카드, 와이페이모어와 AI 에이전트 항공권 결제 실증 발행일 : 2026-11-25 12:32 전자신문을 선호 매체로 추가 공유하기 페이스북 X(트위터) X(트위터) --> 메일 URL 복사 글자크기 설정 가 작게 가 보통 가 크게 KB국민카드는 지난 9월 서울 종로구 KB국민카드 본사에서 에스와이폴라리스와 'AI 에이전트 기반 결제 검증 공동 실증' 업무협약(MOU)를 체결했다. 왼쪽부터 이호준 KB국민카드 디지털사업그룹 전무, 박상만 에스와이폴라리스 대표 에스와이폴라리스는 KB국민카드, 항공권 예약 플랫폼 와이페이모어와 AI 에이전트가 고객을 대신해 항공권을 예약하고 결제하는 공동 실증(PoC)을 진행하고 있다고 25일 밝혔다. 실증에는 와이페이모어가 가맹점으로 참여해, AI 에이전트가 고객의 요청에 따라 항공권을 조회하고 결제하는 과정을 세 회사가 함께 검증한다. 세 회사는 기존 카드사의 인증·결제 체계를 기반으로 AI 에이전트 결제의 적용 가능성을 검증하고, 고객정보 보호와 안전한 결제 환경을 위한 방안도 모색할 예정이다. 실증에는 에스와이폴라리스가 개발한 카드사 기반 AI 에이전트 결제 규격 'K-AP'가 쓰인다. 카드사가 운영해 온 기존 본인인증 체계를 바꾸지 않고, AI 에이전트 확인 단계를 더하는 방식이다. KB국민카드와 에스와이폴라리스가 지난 9월 'AI 에이전트 기반 결제 검증 공동 실증' 협약을 맺은 뒤 진행한 첫 실증이다. 항공권은 운임 변동이 잦고 예약·발권 절차가 복잡해 AI 에이전트의 정확성과 신뢰도 제고를 위해 카드사와 결제 실증을 진행하고 있다. 에스와이폴라리스 관계자는 “AI 에이전트 결제가 널리 쓰이려면 고객이 안심할 수 있는 결제 기반이 먼저 갖춰져야 한다”며 “카드사 인증 인프라 위에서 국내 표준을 함께 만들어가겠다”고 말했다. 김신영 기자 spicyzero@etnews.com

items.fullText: Into the Omniverse: How Developers Turn Ideas Into Simulations With Frontier AI Agents See how developers are combining AI agents with NVIDIA Omniverse libraries to build simulation applications, test physical behavior and guide improvements. November 19, 2026 by NVIDIA Writers 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Your browser doesn't support HTML5 video. Here is a link to the video instead. Turning a simulation idea into a working application means assembling assets, connecting physics and rendering, and checking that the scene behaves as intended. Developers are combining frontier AI models with NVIDIA Omniverse libraries to help carry out that work — building applications for exploring scenarios, investigating failures and improving designs. Developers direct AI agents through natural-language instructions, review results and guide changes. Omniverse libraries provide GPU-accelerated physics, rendering and sensor simulation capabilities. Explore the projects below to see frontier AI models such as GPT-6 Astra at work, and check back for new examples from NVIDIA teams and developers across the ecosystem. Physical AI Paves the Path to Autonomous Industrial Operations 🔗 https://blogs.nvidia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/Nyhamna_footage_take5_30s.mp4 AI agents powered by frontier models pave the way to autonomous operations. They use industrial tools and engineering data to help engineers build digital twins that test plans and processes and evaluate operational decisions. Falkor, a KONGSBERG company, shows how this works in practice. The company’s Falkor Surface platform lets customers turn their computer-aided design and engineering data into facility-scale digital twins using the GPT-6 Astra model. The platform uses NVIDIA Omniverse libraries and NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Server Edition GPUs on Microsoft Azure to enable advanced physics simulation. November 18, 2026 by Justin Walker 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! New NVIDIA RTX Spark compact desktops from ASUS, Dell and MSI are available today, bringing local AI agents, image and video generation, and model fine-tuning to a dedicated Windows PC. With up to 128GB of unified memory and NVIDIA’s AI software stack, these systems provide room for larger local models alongside RTX-accelerated creative and development tools. A dedicated desktop can keep agents and scheduled tasks running while a laptop travels or handles other work. Alongside the new desktops, an expanding software ecosystem brings more creative and development workflows to RTX Spark laptops and compact desktops. Native Windows on Arm applications from Adobe, the NVIDIA DLSS Ray Reconstruction feature in Blender and local generation workflows in ComfyUI expand what creators and developers can do on RTX Spark — all on one Windows PC. A Windows PC Built for Local AI As workflows expand to include local AI models and agents, more work can continue beyond an active editing session — from generating assets to processing long renders or scheduled tasks. RTX Spark compact desktops give developers, creators and AI enthusiasts a dedicated Windows PC for local models and always-on agents. They bring together image and video generation, model fine-tuning, creative applications and development tools in one compact system. Running supported models locally keeps locally processed code and files on the PC and avoids per-token cloud application programming interface (API) charges for those tasks. items.fullText: Ian Buck Kicks Off NVIDIA’s Week at SC26 as Science Enters the Age of Agents At SC26, NVIDIA’s VP of Hyperscale and HPC laid out how researchers can combine simulation, AI and agents to accelerate scientific discovery. November 17, 2026 by Brian Caulfield 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! NVIDIA’s Ian Buck kicked off the company’s week at SC26 in Chicago on Monday with new tools for AI agents, software that can plan experiments, run code and check results on researchers’ own systems. In NVIDIA’s special address, Buck announced Nemotron for Science , the Rubin HPC GPU and an expanded Vera CPU platform for high-performance computing . He also detailed a new collaboration in quantum computing with IBM and Fermi National Accelerator Laboratory . “The frontier of computing and the new scientific stack is going to be simulation, as always, but combined with AI and the future of quantum,” said Buck, vice president of hyperscale and high-performance computing at NVIDIA. Buck opened the talk by looking back to his first public talk on CUDA, at an SC06 tutorial in Tampa, Florida, 20 years ago. NVIDIA now offers more than 1,000 CUDA-X libraries , he said. Open Models for Science Agents “[Agents] have been just a game changer in how we interface with our supercomputers, with our devices, our instruments and how we can do the research,” Buck said. Simulation remains the foundation of scientific computing, “which will always be on the top,” Buck said, with AI, quantum and now agents working alongside it. With expanded NVIDIA CUDA-X libraries, including cuPhoton, cuPotential and cuSpa, researchers can sift through vast amounts of data to accelerate research, from astrophysics and materials science to single-cell biology. The speedups are helping scientists analyze larger datasets and model more complex systems. The new libraries give AI agents the tools to help researchers make discoveries faster than ever. Read All NVIDIA Announcements From SC26 Bringing Black Holes Into Focus Seeing a black hole takes a telescope the size of Earth. The Event Horizon Telescope links radio dishes worldwide, generating petabytes of data that can take months to process. With NVIDIA cuPhoton.xBeam, a module within the cuPhoton Toolkit , black hole observations from the Event Horizon Telescope can now be correlated orders of magnitude faster than ever. Analysis that once took over a month now takes eight minutes. By combining global radio dishes into Earth-sized aperture, cuPhoton delivers unprecedented astronomical imaging resolution. cuPhoton successfully correlated observations of powerful black hole jets J1924 and 3C279 in the night sky — making it a reality to reconstruct a Messier 87* black hole galaxy in real time. The entire pipeline, from data loading and processing to visualization, runs on distributed multi-GPU systems or a compact NVIDIA DGX Spark system, helping scientists study how gas spirals inward under a black hole’s powerful gravitational pull. Steering Fusion Simulations Sustaining plasma at millions of degrees is essential to achieving stable, continuous fusion energy. But simulating its behavior is costly: on petascale systems, a single time step can take days, with simulations running for weeks. items.fullText: AI Day Seoul Brings Together Korea’s Industry Leaders, Startups and Developer Communities November 15, 2026 by NVIDIA Writers 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Over two days at COEX, more than 2,000 attendees converged for AI Day Seoul, bringing together Korea’s industry leaders, startups and developer communities advancing physical AI and AI agents. At the plenary sessions, Deepu Talla, vice president of robotics and edge AI at NVIDIA, said Korea is “punching above its weight,” with Doosan Robotics, Hyundai Motor Group, LG Electronics and SK Group — as well as startups like Real World and Luda Robotics — using NVIDIA platforms to bring general-purpose robotics into the real world. Jonathan Cohen, vice president of applied research at NVIDIA, showed how enterprises can build agents they own and control. Breakout sessions featured speakers from Coupang Intelligent Cloud, Doosan Robotics, LG AI Research, LG Electronics, NAVER Cloud, SK Telecom and Upstage. “It was a genuinely enjoyable time to have candid conversations,” said Hyunho Yang, research engineer for omnimodal foundation models at SK Telecom. “Seeing the passion of fellow AI developers was a real source of inspiration for me.” Community leaders share how they build with open models and tools at AI Day Seoul. The Agentic AI 10x Bootcamp Community Day brought together Pseudo Lab, Python Korea, PyTorchKR, HAERAE, Hugging Face KREW, Graph User Group, Womxn Who Code Korea, Dnol (Datayanolja) and other developer communities. Five finalists from the Hangul Day hackathon, co-hosted with Fastcampus, built agents trained on the Korean language and culture with the OpenShell runtime. The winning team, FlyGate, received an NVIDIA DGX Spark system. More than 500 developers also took part in full-day NVIDIA Deep Learning Institute workshops and NVIDIA Certification exams in Korean.
